notes.title: Forest Ranger Patch 1.6
notes.content:
Hello Rangers!
Due to the bugs you reported, we have decided to update the current version of the game, which fixes some of the bugs you reported. You can find the list of fixed things below! In addition, the reported bugs we will try to fix also welcome reports, including those related to changes in gameplay.

[previewyoutube=NlfBGVcu9y0;full][/previewyoutube]


[Fixed]
[list]
[*] Bug reporter restored (IMPORTANT: If there is a problem with the record please attach the last record and log file)
[*] Corrected display of German and French in ForestWiki
[*] Fixed bug with entering the pop-up menu near the computer
[*] There is no longer an effect on the screen after the hunger bar drops.
[*] Added audio effects after hunger bar drop.
[*] Added notifications after hunger bar drop and thirst bar drop.
[*] Rebalanced and reduced hunger and thirst consumption.
[*] Visual changes to the timer for the start of the tourist season.
[*] Fixed bug with timer stopping when entering the store.
[/list]


In the near future, an update will be added to improve performance and allow gameplay with a gamepad. 

Hope to hear from you soon!

[i]Coming soon this game update: the restoration of a classic Forester's Lodge. Join us on this journey to revive this historic wilderness retreat.[/i]


[h3][b]Key Details about the Forester's Lodge:[/b][/h3]

[b]Architectural Charm:[/b] A rustic structure designed to blend with nature's beauty.

[b]Purpose:[/b] The hub for rangers to monitor wildlife and ensure forest health.

[b]Amenities:[/b] Basic comforts in a natural setting.

[b]Cultural Value:[/b] Reflects the deep connection between people and forests.

[b]Challenges Ahead:[/b] Maintenance and restoration to preserve its legacy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36177732/580af8b3b2f375ac565aebc46c2e718a969422bd.jpg[/img]

[i]Prepare to step into the shoes of a forest ranger and restore a Forester's Lodge in the upcoming update![/i]


[h3][b]The Guardians of Nature: Forest Rangers[/b][/h3]

Forest rangers are the unsung heroes of our natural landscapes. They serve as stewards of the environment, working tirelessly to ensure the well-being of ecosystems within forests and parks. Their responsibilities range from enforcing regulations to monitoring wildlife populations and educating the public about the importance of conservation.

[h3][b]The Importance of Forest Rangers[/b][/h3]

[b]Conservation and Preservation:[/b] Forest rangers are instrumental in safeguarding the flora and fauna of these areas. They monitor and protect endangered species, implementing strategies for ecological restoration.

[b]Fire Management:[/b] Rangers are trained in fire management techniques, working to prevent, control, and mitigate wildfires that can devastate large areas of forests and parks.

[b]Law Enforcement:[/b] Rangers enforce regulations that ensure the safety and well-being of both the environment and park visitors, preventing illegal activities such as poaching and vandalism.

[b]Maintenance and Shelter:[/b] Forest rangers are responsible for maintaining their shelters and infrastructure in the woods, ensuring their functionality and safety, which is vital for their conservation and law enforcement efforts.

Preserving forests and parks, respecting the objects within them, and supporting the efforts of forest rangers are essential steps in ensuring that these areas continue to provide clean air, mental and physical health benefits, recreational opportunities, and educational experiences for generations to come.

As we revel in the beauty of nature, let us also acknowledge and support those who work diligently behind the scenes—forest rangers. They are the guardians of our forests and parks, ensuring that these invaluable natural treasures remain intact for the well-being and enjoyment of all.

notes.title: New mechanics

[h3]Hello Rangers! [/h3]

[u]We are halfway through [b]Kickstarter[/b]. More than [b]200 backers and YouTubers[/b] sent us a lot of feedback and ideas.[/u]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TvNiIwQ.gif[/img]

notes.title: National Forest Day
notes.content:
As everyone knows that Christmas means happiness, relaxation presents, and Christmas Tree.
But many of us don't realize that this is one of the worst days for forests all over the world.

A lot of people buy/cut a beautiful tree that was growing somewhere in the forest which was fighting for us with the pollution, being a shelter for many animals.

Today is [b]NATIONAL FOREST DAY[/b]. Isn't this the best time to do something beneficial for the planet?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36177732/e0b53e50b7182f79d8a06865fcca0a32a91f7d0e.jpg[/img]

We know everyone loves glowing Christmas trees, but what if those who have enough land near their house plant one (or more) trees and then dress it up with baubles and lights for Christmas time?

[b]Our Forest Ranger did that... can you do it?[/b]
